answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks using hardware-rooted attestation. Enclave-bound agents present cryptographic quotes authenticated against vendor roots and challenge nonces from a yarrow PRNG. An attacker incurs the verifiable cost of provisioning physical silicon per identity, dispelling the fable of zero-cost replication while ensuring no relic quote is reused. However, this approach centralizes supply-chain trust and remains vulnerable to microarchitectural side-channel leaks.
